MCP Console lets your agent run R, Python, and SQL, inspect live objects, and refine its work after seeing the results.
Data and models stay in memory between calls, so a follow-up question can use what the agent has already computed.

Code runs in an [OS-level sandbox](SANDBOX.md) by default, with configurable limits on filesystem writes and direct network access.
By default, Console prepares environments and packages automatically; no Console configuration file is required.

## Work in a persistent session

Console provides a persistent session—a REPL—through one MCP tool, `send`.

For example, during exploratory data analysis, the agent can load a dataset, fit a model, and plot the residuals.
If something looks wrong, it can inspect intermediate results or refine the plot using the data and model already in memory.

The agent can also:

- Read help, pause in a debugger, and evaluate code against live objects.
- Run long computations across calls and collect output as it arrives.
- Interrupt work and keep the session, or [restart it](SEND_OPERATIONS.md#explicit-restart) to clear live objects and start fresh.
- Read previews of long output that limit how much text enters the model's context.
- Revisit logs and plots through [recordings](RECORDING.md).

## R, Python, and SQL {#one-workspace-three-languages}

The built-in runtimes are embedded in one process, so the agent can pass data between R, Python, and SQL without writing intermediate files.
It can use one language or combine them in the same session.
See [Working with R, Python, and SQL](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md).

## Environment setup

By default, Console prepares packages and extensions for the session:

- **R packages** go into ephemeral, cache-backed libraries layered on top of the host's R libraries.
- **Python packages** go into an ephemeral, cache-backed Python environment.
- **DuckDB extensions** are installed in a reusable cache for the session's in-memory database.

Cached installations persist after a session ends and can be reused in later sessions.
The agent can request additional packages and extensions as it works.
You can instead [use a preconfigured Python environment](CONFIGURATION.md#python-environment-selection), which disables managed Python preparation, or [disable R package resolution](CONFIGURATION.md#dependency-resolution-policies).
See [Get started](getting-started.qmd) for installation prerequisites and client setup, or [Requirements and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md) for package preparation.

Console works with MCP-compatible clients such as Codex and Claude Code and does not depend on a particular model provider.

## Where Console fits

- **Unattended analysis:** run long analyses with limits on where the agent can write files and connect to the network.
- **Model evaluations:** evaluate how an agent explores data, checks its work, and responds to results.
- **Conversational analysis:** discuss questions and results while the agent runs the analysis in its own session.
- **Large datasets:** keep data and intermediate results in memory for follow-up questions.
- **Debugging and package development:** pause execution, inspect live objects, and evaluate code where a failure occurs.

## Status and trust

Console is a **development preview** for macOS, Linux, and [experimental Windows x64](WINDOWS.md).
Run it alongside the MCP client on the intended execution host.

The default sandbox permits regular-file writes only in private temporary storage and restricts direct networking, but permits host-file reads.
**Readable secrets are not protected.** Project configuration is trusted input and may widen permissions.
Dependency preparation has a separate policy.
Recordings contain input and output without redaction and have no automatic cleanup.
See [Sandbox and trust](SANDBOX.md) before changing permissions and [Recordings and reports](RECORDING.md) before sharing session files.
